business_purpose: If a condition is a PED, the specific health plan may apply a PED waiting period before the PED waiting-period restriction ends. The actual waiting period, any continuity or portability credit, and any claim outcome must come from the applicable product terms and customer documents.
calculation_basis: Apply the governed 36-month look-back in the PED definition. Do not infer a product-specific waiting period, claim approval, or claim payment.
constraints: This record explains the generic PED definition only.
It does not state any insurer-specific or product-specific PED waiting period.
It does not determine customer-specific PED status without the relevant dates and medical history.
It does not determine claim admissibility, approval, payment, entitlement, or recommendation.
The applicable PED waiting-period duration, optional modifications, continuity or portability credit, exclusions, and other product mechanics must come from governed product knowledge.

Customer-specific policy dates, prior continuous coverage, selected options, endorsements, declarations, and relevant medical history must be verified from the applicable customer documents before applying the rule to that customer.
core_meaning: A Pre-Existing Disease (PED) means any condition, ailment, injury or disease that was diagnosed by a physician not more than 36 months before the policy commencement date, or for which medical advice or treatment was recommended or received from a physician not more than 36 months before policy commencement.

exceptions: No generic exception is asserted. Product-specific treatment of PEDs must come from governed product and customer-document evidence.
functional_behaviour: A Pre-Existing Disease (PED) is a health problem or medical condition you already had before your insurance started. Under the formal definition used here, the relevant look-back is 36 months for diagnosis, medical advice or treatment.
